THE_NEW_FINDING.headline: The production walk is red for a reason nothing in this wave predicted, and it is NOT S13 and NOT fixable by the S13 fix. On production the 16 hollow Bastrop nodes grade BP-MEANING-01 FAIL with reason 'HTTP 404'. On staging the SAME 16 nodes grade RETIRED PASS. The whole difference is a serve-side predicate that is live in production and not in staging.

measuredGradeDivergence.reading: identical 86-parcel walk, identical 69 plain passes, identical 1 BP-VERIFY-01 pass, sFamilies clean on BOTH. The ONLY difference is the 16: RETIRED/pass on staging, BP-MEANING-01/fail on production. Nothing about the DATA differs -- both walks ran the same digest against the same county.

theMechanism.evidence1_verbatimPerParcel: every one of the 16 rows in walk_results reads: {"grade": "BP-MEANING-01", "reason": "HTTP 404", "sGrades": {"S1": PASS, "S2": UNMEASURED, "S3": UNMEASURED, ...}} -- the reason is literally the string 'HTTP 404'. The walk is not grading a defect in the record; it is grading the serve-side refusal.
theMechanism.evidence2_theDecline: the 404 body is not_baked/no_coverage, emitted at exactly one place -- brokerageNodeFacets.ts:880-885 -- and reached because shouldDeclineRetiredRecordAtServe(parcelNodeId, row.payloadJson) returns true. LANDUSE_JOIN_DISABLED_FIPS_SEED = {48491, 48209} (joinNormalize.ts:93); 48209 is in it; the row's retirement is an earned retirement. The row is PRESENT in the store at the run id this walk just wrote, and is deliberately DISCARDED before the route answers.
theMechanism.evidence3_whyStagingDiffers: the same predicate run against the same parcels must produce the same 404 on staging, so the fact that staging served them (retiredCount 16, RETIRED pass) means staging's cortex-api revision does NOT apply the decline. Production cortex-api runs 00799-xaq (LDT 8f91d5d1) and has the predicate; the staging serving revision does not.
theMechanism.soTheChain: bake writes an earned retirement -> production serve DECLINES it (404) -> the walk reads through the serve, sees no row -> grades BP-MEANING-01 fail -> the walk is RED. The retirement pass and the serve decline are two halves of P-180 and they are in direct conflict with each other at the walk.

THE_NEW_FINDING.consequence: No production publish of a gate-blocked county (48209, 48491) can produce a green walk today, at any LDT SHA, with any of the fixes in this wave. The S13 fix was necessary and it worked -- S13 failures went 16 -> 0 and sFamilies is empty -- but BP-MEANING-01 now carries the same 16 rows across the line. We did not fix the walk; we moved the failure.
THE_NEW_FINDING.theShapeOfTheFix: the walk needs the companion change to the S13 fix, on the SAME 16-row population: a declined earned retirement (404 + not_baked/no_coverage on a parcel whose record is an earned retirement) must be an ACCEPTABLE served outcome -- the same reasoning that made S13 land on UNMEASURED, because a row that by construction serves no provenance should not be graded as if it served nothing. It must be written so it cannot silence a genuine no-coverage 404, and the two-directional tests must show both directions, exactly as PR #149's did.

SECOND_FINDING_theSiblingIsNotFaithful.statement: requireStagingSibling is the guard that gates a production publish on a passing STAGING walk -- and staging does not run the serve predicate that decides the walk's verdict in a gate-blocked county. The guard's input is measured on a different serve path than the thing it guards.
SECOND_FINDING_theSiblingIsNotFaithful.whyItMatters: on this very run the guard was satisfied (staging sibling 5b3a1c2c, staging walk 8eacb135 PASS) and the production walk then failed. The guard did its job as written; the staging environment is simply not a faithful sibling for this predicate. A staging-green walk is not evidence that a production walk will be green.
SECOND_FINDING_theSiblingIsNotFaithful.relationshipToTheTrustGap: this is NOT a reopening of the walk-verdict trust gap the operator recorded as satisfied -- that gap was about whether the staging walk's PASS was real, and it is real and independently confirmed (the coordinator's requireStagingSibling SQL cleared all six checks at 16:11:31Z, and the lane's own reads agree). This is a different, narrower claim: the staging PASS is genuine AND it does not transfer, because the environments differ in the one predicate that decides these 16 rows.
SECOND_FINDING_theSiblingIsNotFaithful.doNotOverstate: this is measured for 48209/48491 (the decline's hardcoded county set). For counties outside {48491, 48209} the guard's premise is unaffected -- the predicate returns false immediately on the countyFips check, which is why 48055:1 (Caldwell, retired, same shape) serves 200.

It writes parcel_gate_verdict, which is what PARCEL-B-READER consumes to decide whether a rail serves record or fails closed to legacy-transitional, i.e. exactly the served state the walk grades.
